result.summary: This PR adds a new test-framework feature, auto_outbound_mode, which lets functional tests transparently redirect a node's SOCKS5-proxied outbound connections to controlled Python peers, so tests can exercise connections the node itself decides to make (as opposed to test-initiated connections). It then adds a new functional test, p2p_outbound_management.py, covering stale-tip extra outbound connections, periodic block-relay-only reconnects, and per-network outbound diversification, and refactors p2p_private_broadcast.py to reuse the new framework code, cutting significant duplication.
result.problem: Existing functional tests can only simulate outbound connections that the test itself initiates; there was no good way to test the node's own automatic outbound-connection decisions (stale-tip handling, periodic block-relay reconnects, network diversification), leaving these behaviors under-tested. This affects test coverage of p2p connection-management logic maintained by reviewers like vasild and mzumsande.

open_concerns: Author had an intermittent local test failure in p2p_private_broadcast.py after the latest rebase that needs investigation.
Design questions around auto_outbound_factory interface (index-only vs also passing requested address/port, per vasild referencing #34410) remain open but non-blocking.
Bortlesboat asked for a comment explaining the '46' scheduler-interval magic number; not yet confirmed addressed.

Multiple naming/API-shape suggestions (auto_outbound_factory, decide_auto_outbound_where_to) were implemented by the author.
Concerns about ordering of tor/cjdns connection setup vs addrman population were addressed by restructuring the test's address-adding sequence.

result.card: This PR adds a reusable test-framework feature, auto_outbound_mode, letting functional tests intercept and redirect a node's own automatically-initiated outbound connections via a SOCKS5 proxy, and uses it to add a new functional test covering stale-tip extra outbounds, periodic block-relay reconnects, and per-network outbound diversification (all pre-existing, already-merged behaviors). It also refactors p2p_private_broadcast.py to reuse the new framework code, removing significant duplication. Two reviewers, vasild (the original author of the underlying proxy-redirection mechanism) and Bortlesboat, gave full ACKs on earlier revisions after testing locally, with all design feedback addressed across many rounds. However, after a rebase in August 2026 the author said the PR is 'not ready for review yet - still need to change some things', so it is currently paused pending further author work despite the prior positive reviews. No PR dependencies are stated, though it deliberately builds on patterns from #29415 and #34186.
